rationale: Empirical mixed-methods study (surveys of 400 slum residents in Bengaluru and 500 rural residents in North Karnataka plus FGDs and case studies) examining household/community toilet access, usage, and open defecation (C1, C3, C4 met). While the abstract highlights technical, behavioural, water-scarcity, cultural, space, and financial barriers alongside broad references to 'improved governance' and 'institutionalising the process of construction with transparency and accountability', full-text review is required under the narrow Criterion 2 reading to determine whether concrete administrative, subsidy-delivery, municipal O&M, or slum-tenure rules are empirically analysed rather than generic project delivery and behavioural factors.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the plain Criterion 2 wording, the study's focus on improved governance, operation and maintenance, and institutionalising toilet construction with transparency and accountability across slum and rural sanitation interventions meets the broad institutional/governance threshold ('include'). Under the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, generic governance and construction-process recommendations would not suffice on their own, but because the study empirically investigates 20 urban slums, financial constraints, and state sanitation interventions where tenure, subsidy eligibility/disbursement, or municipal administrative rules may be analysed in the full text, it is retained as 'unsure' for full-text verification.

evidence_quotes.quote: We surveyed 400 respondents across 20 slums and 500 respondents in six districts of North Karnataka through survey instruments and focus group discussions (FGDs) to understand the problems with respect to toilet access and usage.
This paper captures these issues in-depth and provides some options in technologies and improved governance based on study findings and review of case studies.
Also, institutionalising the process of construction with transparency and accountability at various stages matters to ensure proper construction of toilets.
